attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised proposition keeps the 'probably' hedge on the human 90%+ figure and the scope to NYT Connections. The firm part that can be scored is that current models aren't close, which is an observation about the time of the post.

contract.note: The contract scores only the firm claim that models aren't close and leaves out the hedged human estimate. It reads 'current' as the April 2024 snapshot and 'aren't close' as a substantial gap. That is an ordinary plain reading. Marcus himself cited Mazur's benchmark, so it is the right measure.

evidence.note: Mazur's own benchmark results, dated April 4, 2024, within the target period. The top scores are GPT-4 Turbo at 31.0 and Claude 3 Opus at 27.3, and all other models score lower. The scoring formula isn't stated, and the April 9 Turbo checkpoint isn't covered. Even so, these scores are far below roughly 90%.

reviews.rationale: Marcus's firm claim was that current models weren't close to roughly 90% on Connections. The benchmark creator's April 4, 2024 results show leading models at 31.0 and 27.3, which is a substantial gap on what appears to be a percentage-style scale. Remaining gaps: the scoring formula isn't given, the comment was edited, and there is no result for the April 9 checkpoint. No evidence suggests any model of that time came near 90%. The hedged human estimate is not scored.
